answer: Make grading seats a commit-reveal lottery: each epoch a reviewer locks a small bond in a vault, commits a hidden score, and reveals only after the jury closes. Seats are drawn from the whole identity graph, so a sybil island cannot route its answers to friendly graders; to forge a passing majority on one answer it must hold most seats, meaning bonds on roughly half the active set. Graders who stray far from the revealed median lose their bond, so collusion costs stake times seats bought.
